project.name: National Integrated Healthcare Ecosystem (NIHE)
project.department: Ministry of Health - Digital Health Division
project.methodology: Hybrid (Agile delivery within phased Waterfall governance gates)
project.geographic_scope: Republic of Uganda (all 146 districts), phased rollout, architected for future East African Community expansion

vision.statement: To create a secure, interoperable, GIS-enabled healthcare ecosystem that connects patients, healthcare providers, regulators, and researchers through a unified digital platform across Uganda.
vision.mission: To digitize and integrate healthcare services, improve accessibility, enable emergency response coordination, support telemedicine, enhance regulatory oversight, protect patient data, and facilitate national health analytics through a single, scalable, and sustainable platform.

objectives.description: Digitize healthcare records and enable seamless sharing across facilities
objectives.measurable_criteria: Patient record retrieval time ≤ 2 seconds; 100% of registered facilities using EHR

objectives.description: Improve healthcare accessibility through GIS-enabled facility discovery and navigation
objectives.measurable_criteria: 100% of districts covered; facility location accuracy ≤ 10m

objectives.description: Enable emergency response coordination with real-time dispatch and tracking
objectives.measurable_criteria: Emergency dispatch time ≤ 2 minutes; patient location accuracy ≤ 50m

objectives.description: Support telemedicine services for remote consultation and care
objectives.measurable_criteria: Video consultation connection success rate ≥ 95%; patient satisfaction ≥ 4/5

objectives.description: Improve regulatory oversight through compliance monitoring and pharmacovigilance
objectives.measurable_criteria: Regulatory compliance rate 100%; ADR report acknowledgment ≤ 4 hours

objectives.description: Enable national health analytics and public health surveillance
objectives.measurable_criteria: Surveillance data freshness ≤ 5 minutes; outbreak detection ≤ 48 hours

objectives.description: Facilitate interoperability with existing healthcare systems
objectives.measurable_criteria: HL7/FHIR standards compliance ≥ 95%; integration success rate ≥ 95%

objectives.description: Protect patient data privacy and platform security through robust cybersecurity controls and compliance
objectives.measurable_criteria: Zero critical (Severity 1) security incidents per year; 100% of facilities completing annual security awareness training; full compliance verified in annual Data Protection Act audits

objectives.description: Build sustainable digital health capacity among healthcare workers and facility administrators
objectives.measurable_criteria: ≥ 90% of onboarded healthcare personnel certified on platform use within 60 days of facility go-live; digital health literacy training delivered in all 146 districts

in_scope: Patient-facing services: account management, EHR access, appointment booking, telemedicine, AI health assistant, facility discovery and navigation, emergency assistance, online pharmacy, payments, health monitoring, medication reminders, pharmacovigilance reporting, reviews and notifications

Health facility services: registration and verification, staff and patient management, EMR, telemedicine, pharmacy and laboratory operations, order and delivery management, emergency services, location and mapping, financial management, reviews, pharmacovigilance, reporting, and notifications

Healthcare personnel services: professional profile management, availability and scheduling, patient search and access, clinical consultation management, telemedicine, prescription management, laboratory and diagnostic requests, referral management, emergency response, pharmacist and laboratory functions, care coordination, pharmacovigilance, health monitoring, reviews, reporting, and notifications

System administration: user, facility, and personnel lifecycle management; content and catalog governance; transaction oversight; security and audit administration; system configuration; monitoring; backup and recovery

Regulatory oversight: facility and personnel oversight; prescription and medicine oversight; pharmacovigilance management; public health surveillance; inspection management; complaint investigation; national health analytics
Audit capabilities: audit trail management; compliance auditing; financial auditing; security auditing
Developer ecosystem: REST and GraphQL APIs; webhooks; SDKs; plugin framework; healthcare interoperability standards (HL7, FHIR, ICD, SNOMED CT, LOINC)
GIS capabilities: facility geocoding; map tile services; routing and navigation; geospatial analytics; emergency location services

Security, privacy, and compliance services: end-to-end encryption, encryption key management, consent management, role-based access control, access auditing, and data subject rights handling under Uganda's Data Protection and Privacy Act

Capacity building and support: healthcare-worker digital literacy training, facility administrator onboarding, multi-channel help desk and support services, district-level adoption dashboards, and a monitoring & evaluation framework
out_of_scope: Integration with government identity systems not yet available
Insurance platform integration, including national health insurance claims processing and adjudication (future phase)
USSD gateway for feature phones (future phase)
Wearable device integration beyond commercially available APIs
Cross-border (East African Community) health data exchange (planned for a future regional-expansion phase; current architecture is designed to support it but exchange is not activated in this phase)
scope.boundaries: The system is designed for national-scale deployment within Uganda, with architecture supporting future East African expansion. It is an API-first, headless-capable platform that exposes all core functionality through documented APIs consumed by web, mobile, and third-party clients. The implementation phase concludes with a structured post-go-live stabilization (hypercare) period before full operational handover to a permanent Ministry of Health ICT and Digital Health Division team.

constraints: Must operate under low-bandwidth conditions (≤ 100 Kbps) representative of rural Uganda
Must support intermittent connectivity with offline capabilities for critical functions
Must comply with Uganda's Data Protection and Privacy Act and healthcare regulatory requirements administered by the Ministry of Health and National Drug Authority
Must support Mobile Money as a primary payment method
Must support HL7/FHIR interoperability standards for integration with existing systems
Must be deployable on cloud, on-premises, or hybrid infrastructure
Must support 99.9% uptime for all critical services
Must support patient-facing content in English, Luganda, Runyankole, Luo, and other major Ugandan languages
Must comply with Uganda's Public Procurement and Disposal of Public Assets Authority (PPDA) regulations for all hardware, software, and vendor contracts
assumptions: Patients, healthcare personnel, and facility staff have access to internet-connected smartphones, tablets, or computers, even if connectivity is intermittent or low-bandwidth
Healthcare facilities and personnel onboarding possess valid licensure and legal authority to deliver registered services
Cooperation from healthcare facilities and regulatory bodies (MoH, NDA) for credential verification is available
Third-party Mobile Money, SMS, email, and mapping service providers maintain acceptable service levels
Future integration with government identity, insurance, and national health systems will be possible
The platform will achieve sufficient adoption to realize national-scale benefits
National electricity supply and data-center infrastructure will provide sufficient reliability for primary and backup hosting sites
The Ministry of Health will provide sustained budgetary support beyond the initial implementation period for ongoing operations and maintenance
success_criteria: National facility mapping coverage 100% of districts
100% of registered healthcare facilities using the platform
Zero critical (Severity 1) security incidents during the first 12 months post-launch
≥ 90% of onboarded healthcare personnel digitally certified on platform use
Help desk first-response time ≤ 30 minutes during business hours

risks.description: Limited internet connectivity in rural areas may reduce platform adoption and usability
risks.mitigation: Implement offline-first architecture, data compression, USSD fallback, and progressive web app capabilities

risks.description: Resistance to digital adoption from healthcare workers and facilities
risks.mitigation: Comprehensive training programs, stakeholder engagement, pilot testing, user-centred design

risks.description: Data privacy and security breaches compromising patient information
risks.mitigation: End-to-end encryption, role-based access control, regular security audits, compliance with Uganda Data Protection Act

risks.description: Interoperability challenges with existing healthcare systems
risks.mitigation: Adopt HL7/FHIR standards, provide integration SDKs, API-first architecture, partner engagement

risks.description: Project funding constraints may impact scope or timeline
risks.mitigation: Phased delivery approach, prioritise core functionality, secure government and donor funding

risks.description: Regulatory changes affecting healthcare data handling or telemedicine
risks.mitigation: Engage regulators early, build flexible compliance framework, regular legal review

risks.description: Insufficient GIS data quality for routing and facility location
risks.mitigation: Ground-truthing validation, community mapping partnerships, leverage OpenStreetMap

risks.description: Cybersecurity threats, including ransomware and data breaches, targeting national health infrastructure
risks.mitigation: Defense-in-depth security architecture, 24/7 security operations monitoring, regular penetration testing, documented incident response plan, cyber insurance

risks.description: Attrition of key technical personnel (architects, GIS specialists, security leads) during the project lifecycle
risks.mitigation: Competitive retention packages, thorough knowledge documentation, cross-training, succession planning, partnerships with local universities for talent pipeline

risks.description: Over-dependence on third-party vendors (cloud, payment, mapping) creating lock-in or service-continuity risk
risks.mitigation: Multi-vendor strategy where feasible, contractual SLAs, data portability requirements, defined exit clauses in vendor contracts

risks.description: Poor data quality and migration errors when importing legacy paper-based or fragmented digital records
risks.mitigation: Pre-migration data quality audits, phased data validation, dedicated data migration team, tested rollback procedures
